claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by dynamic formation and self-healing of a protective tribo-oxide film.
Al and Ti enhance the stability of the protective tribo-oxide film.
The tribo-oxide film reduces mechanical material removal during sliding.
The tribo-oxide film reduces electrochemical dissolution during sliding in corrosive media.
The initial alloy is CoCrFeNi.
The proposed intervention adds 0.5 at% Al and 0.2 at% Ti to CoCrFeNi.
The modified alloy is designated CoCrFeNiAl0.5Ti0.2.
Al and Ti additions produce an adherent, self-healing, Al- and Ti-enriched oxide tribo-film on the sliding surface.
Al and Ti promote rapid repassivation after mechanical disruption.
Al and Ti form a dense oxide layer that impedes plowing and wear.
The dense oxide layer impedes anodic metal dissolution.
The proposed oxide-mediated effects reduce synergistic wear-corrosion degradation.
Under the specified test conditions, the modified alloy will have approximately 30% lower combined wear-plus-corrosion loss than CoCrFeNi.
Under the specified test conditions, the modified alloy will have approximately 20% lower wear-only volume loss than CoCrFeNi.
Under the specified test conditions, the modified alloy will have approximately 50% lower steady-state corrosion current density than CoCrFeNi.
The prediction should hold at pH values of at least 6 and sliding speeds no greater than 10 mm/s.
The prediction should fail at pH values of 4 or lower because acid attack overwhelms the oxide's protective ability.
The effect-size estimates are extrapolated from passive-film studies.
Direct wear-corrosion synergy data are lacking for this specific alloy system.
The hypothesis is falsified if the modified alloy shows less than a 10% reduction in combined material loss and no measurable improvement in oxide-film continuity or Al/Ti enrichment.

contradictions.description: The stated additions of 0.5 at% Al and 0.2 at% Ti are inconsistent with the conventional interpretation of the formula CoCrFeNiAl0.5Ti0.2. As molar-ratio notation, that formula corresponds to approximately 10.64 at% Al and 4.26 at% Ti, not 0.5 at% and 0.2 at%.
